"inputs," "observed output," "operator note," and "compatibility limit" is
inside the fixed boilerplate `note`/`Evidence` sentence described below —
none of these are present as actual recorded values anywhere in any source.

## Note/Evidence text is a single fixed template across all files

Every case row in every file (748 rows total: 148 + 156 + 145 + 149 + 166)
matches this exact sentence, confirmed with a single regex applied to all
five files and counting exactly one match per case row in each file (counts
matched each file's total case-row count with no remainder):

> "Recorded restart-safe account recovery retries evidence for architecture
> decision review. The archived evidence marks this case as `{status}` on
> `{platform}`. The review records stated inputs, observed output, operator
> note, and compatibility limit."

Only `{status}` and `{platform}` vary, and they vary in lockstep with the
fixed 4-cycle described above — never independently. No source row contains
a concrete input value, output value, operator name/note, or compatibility
limit value; the sentence only asserts that such things were recorded
elsewhere, without stating them.

## Other confirmed characteristics

- All five files are plain ASCII text with no CRLF line endings (`grep -c

- `request-cedar-lane.jsonl` is valid JSON Lines (`file` reports "JSON

- `tenant-silver-pine.csv` has a single well-formed 4-column header

## Open questions

1. None of the five sources states what "restart-safe" behavior was
   actually being verified (e.g., no request/response payloads, no retry

   compatibility limit" as if these were captured per case, but none of the
   five files contains them. Is there an additional, undiscovered source
   that holds the actual per-case values, or were they never captured?

   platform. Does the absence of failure data mean no failures occurred, or
   that failure data is tracked elsewhere / was not carried into this
   archive?
4. All five files encode the same 4-cycle of (status, platform) pairs
   differing only in total row count and format (Markdown, log, JSONL,
   YAML, CSV) and share one identical timestamp. Are these five files
   independent evidence sources, or export/reformat copies of one
   underlying dataset? The sources do not state their provenance or
   relationship to one another.
5. `identity-north-star.md` case rows use "case N" as bare text within a
   bullet, while the other four files use a colon-delimited `filename:N`
   locator inside a structured field. Was this format difference
   intentional, or is it an artifact of how each file was produced?

All content under `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/` is templated
placeholder-style text: identical boilerplate wording across five different

`restart-quiet-river.yaml:`, `tenant-silver-pine.csv:`). Every case row in
every file references only its own filename — no cross-file identifiers were
found in any source.

## Status and platform fields

Each source row carries a `status` and a `platform` field (field names differ
by format: `Status:`/`Platform:` in the Markdown file, `status=`/`platform=`
in the log, `status`/`platform` JSON keys in the JSONL file, `status:`/`platform:`
in the YAML file, and `status`/`platform` CSV columns).

Observed values, identical across all five files:

- **Status**: `review`, `documented`, `follow-up`, `compatible`
- **Platform**: `linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `freebsd-x86_64`, `macos-arm64`

Every file cycles these four (status, platform) pairs in the same fixed,
repeating order, starting at case 1 in every file:

1. `linux-x86_64` / `review`
2. `windows-x86_64` / `documented`
3. `freebsd-x86_64` / `follow-up`
4. `macos-arm64` / `compatible`

This was confirmed per file by grouping and counting every
(status, platform) pair present (`grep -oE ... | sort | uniq -c`):

| Source file | freebsd-x86_64/follow-up | linux-x86_64/review | macos-arm64/compatible | windows-x86_64/documented | Total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `identity-north-star.md` | 37 | 37 | 37 | 37 | 148 |
| `mailbox-blue-harbor.log` | 39 | 39 | 39 | 39 | 156 |
| `request-cedar-lane.jsonl` | 36 | 37 | 36 | 36 | 145 |
| `restart-quiet-river.yaml` | 37 | 38 | 37 | 37 | 149 |
| `tenant-silver-pine.csv` | 41 | 42 | 41 | 42 | 166 |

The non-multiple-of-4 totals (145, 149, 166) produce uneven counts because
the fixed 4-case cycle is truncated wherever a file's total case count is not
divisible by 4; the extra case(s) always land on the position(s) earliest in
the cycle (`linux-x86_64`/`review` first, `windows-x86_64`/`documented`
second where a second extra exists). No row in any file was found that
deviates from the fixed 4-cycle order or introduces a fifth status or
platform value.

## Case and failure search

Searched all five files (case-insensitive) for `failure`, `error`, `crash`,
and `exception`, and for the word-bounded token `fail` (which would also
match `fail-...` variants without matching `follow-up`): **zero matches** in
every file. No source contains a failure record, error record, or any
narrative distinguishing one case's outcome from another beyond the four
`status` values listed above.

Searched all five files for JSON/structured keys named `inputs`, `output`,
`operator`, or `limit`: **zero matches**. The only appearance of the words
"inputs," "observed output," "operator note," and "compatibility limit" is
inside the fixed boilerplate `note`/`Evidence` sentence described below —
none of these are present as actual recorded values anywhere in any source.

## Note/Evidence text is a single fixed template across all files

Every case row in every file (748 rows total: 148 + 156 + 145 + 149 + 166)
matches this exact sentence, confirmed with a single regex applied to all
five files and counting exactly one match per case row in each file (counts
matched each file's total case-row count with no remainder):

> "Recorded restart-safe account recovery retries evidence for architecture
> decision review. The archived evidence marks this case as `{status}` on
> `{platform}`. The review records stated inputs, observed output, operator
> note, and compatibility limit."

Only `{status}` and `{platform}` vary, and they vary in lockstep with the
fixed 4-cycle described above — never independently. No source row contains
a concrete input value, output value, operator name/note, or compatibility
limit value; the sentence only asserts that such things were recorded
elsewhere, without stating them.

## Other confirmed characteristics

- All five files are plain ASCII text with no CRLF line endings (`grep -c
  $'\r'` returned 0 matches for every file).
- All five files share the same file size class (~51 KB, `ls -la`) and the
  same last-modified timestamp (`Aug 26 14:31`) — consistent with having
  been generated together as a set, though the sources do not state this.
- `request-cedar-lane.jsonl` is valid JSON Lines (`file` reports "JSON
  data"); each line parses independently.
- `tenant-silver-pine.csv` has a single well-formed 4-column header
  (`case,platform,status,note`) followed only by data rows.

## Open questions

1. None of the five sources states what "restart-safe" behavior was
   actually being verified (e.g., no request/response payloads, no retry
   counts, no timing data). What system behavior did each `status` value
   (`review`, `documented`, `follow-up`, `compatible`) originally certify?
2. The sources reference "stated inputs, observed output, operator note, and
   compatibility limit" as if these were captured per case, but none of the
   five files contains them. Is there an additional, undiscovered source
   that holds the actual per-case values, or were they never captured?
3. No source contains a failure, error, or incompatibility record for any
   platform. Does the absence of failure data mean no failures occurred, or
   that failure data is tracked elsewhere / was not carried into this
   archive?
4. All five files encode the same 4-cycle of (status, platform) pairs
   differing only in total row count and format (Markdown, log, JSONL,
   YAML, CSV) and share one identical timestamp. Are these five files
   independent evidence sources, or export/reformat copies of one
   underlying dataset? The sources do not state their provenance or
   relationship to one another.
5. `identity-north-star.md` case rows use "case N" as bare text within a
   bullet, while the other four files use a colon-delimited `filename:N`
   locator inside a structured field. Was this format difference
   intentional, or is it an artifact of how each file was produced?

## Handoff note

All content under `maintenance/inputs/architecture-decisions/` is templated
placeholder-style text: identical boilerplate wording across five different
file formats, a fixed 4-case (status, platform) cycle with no exceptions,
and no concrete inputs, outputs, operator notes, compatibility limits, or
failure records despite the note text claiming those were recorded. Before
this material is used to support an actual architecture decision for
restart-safe account recovery retries, the open questions above should be
resolved — in particular, whether real per-case evidence exists elsewhere.
As archived, these five files are only sufficient to confirm which
(status, platform) pairs are represented and how many rows exist per file;
they are not sufficient to justify a compatibility or readiness decision on
their own. This review made no changes to `accountsvc/` or `tests/`.

# Account Recovery Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local account and MFA recovery service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes `POST /recovery/start`,
`POST /recovery/complete`, and authenticated
`POST /recovery/notifications/retry`. Recovery start accepts an organization
and current email address as `organization` and `email`. Recovery completion
accepts `token`. Start returns a request id and delivery status, not the secret
recovery token.

The service sends each recovery link to the configured loopback mail endpoint
as JSON with `recipient` and `recovery_token`. A non-success response leaves a
durable notification for later retry. Failed provider responses keep a recovery
locator in `accountsvc.notice`. `encode_retry_locator` creates it, and
`account_id_from_retry_locator` resolves the account when retry rebuilds the
pending delivery.

A recovery token is secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one account
and organization when the service creates it. Email lookup selects the account
only at recovery start. A later email change never changes which account the
token can recover.

An account may release an old email address during an explicit change. Another
account in the same organization may then claim it. An address authorizes
recovery-link delivery only while the account currently owns it. Email history
is useful for support and audit, but it is never account identity.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, storage,
account administration, recovery flow, notification delivery, loopback HTTP
service, and tests.

1	"""Business logic tying storage, models, and mail delivery together.
2	
3	This module implements the documented behaviors:
4	
5	* Recovery tokens are secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one
6	  account and organization at creation time. Email lookup happens only at
7	  recovery start; a later email change never changes which account a token
8	  recovers.
9	* An address only authorizes recovery-link delivery while an account
10	  currently owns it, so notification delivery always resolves the recipient
11	  from the account's *current* email at send time -- including on retry,
12	  after `accountsvc.notice` rebuilds the pending delivery's account binding.
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import hashlib
17	import secrets
18	import uuid
19	
20	from . import notice
21	from .errors import NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
22	from .mailer import send_recovery_mail
23	from .models import RecoveryRequest, validate_email, validate_id
24	from .storage import Storage
25	from .timeutil import future_iso, now_iso
26	
27	RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900
28	
29	
30	def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
31	    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
32	
33	
34	def create_account(storage: Storage, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
35	    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
36	    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
37	    validate_email(email)
38	    account = storage.create_account(org_id, account_id, email)
39	    return account_to_dict(account)
40	
41	
42	def change_email(storage: Storage, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
43	    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
44	    validate_email(new_email)
45	    account = storage.change_email(account_id, new_email)
46	    return account_to_dict(account)
47	
48	
49	def show_account(storage: Storage, account_id: str) -> dict:
50	    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
51	    account = storage.get_account(account_id)
52	    history = storage.get_email_history(account_id)
53	    mfa = storage.get_mfa_enrollment(account_id)
54	    return {
55	        "account_id": account.account_id,
56	        "org_id": account.org_id,
57	        "current_email": account.current_email,
58	        "created_at": account.created_at,
59	        "mfa_enrolled": mfa.enrolled,
60	        "email_history": [
61	            {
62	                "email": entry.email,
63	                "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
64	                "effective_to": entry.effective_to,
65	                "released": entry.released,
66	            }
67	            for entry in history
68	        ],
69	    }
70	
71	
72	def account_to_dict(account) -> dict:
73	    return {
74	        "account_id": account.account_id,
75	        "org_id": account.org_id,
76	        "current_email": account.current_email,
77	        "created_at": account.created_at,
78	    }
79	
80	
81	def start_recovery(storage: Storage, org_id: str, email: str, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
82	    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
83	    validate_email(email)
84	
85	    account = storage.find_account_by_current_email(org_id, email)
86	    if account is None:
87	        raise NotFoundError(
88	            f"no account in organization '{org_id}' currently uses email '{email}'"
89	        )
90	
91	    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
92	    request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
93	    created_at = now_iso()
94	    expires_at = future_iso(RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS)
95	
96	    request = RecoveryRequest(
97	        request_id=request_id,
98	        account_id=account.account_id,
99	        org_id=org_id,
100	        token_hash=_hash_token(token),
101	        token_plain=token,
102	        created_at=created_at,
103	        expires_at=expires_at,
104	        used_at=None,
105	    )
106	    storage.create_recovery_request(request)
107	
108	    success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(mail_endpoint, email, token)
109	    retry_locator = None
110	    if not success:
111	        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
112	    storage.record_notification_attempt(
113	        request_id=request_id,
114	        account_id=account.account_id,
115	        endpoint=mail_endpoint,
116	        success=success,
117	        receipt=receipt,
118	        retry_locator=retry_locator,
119	    )
120	
121	    return {
122	        "request_id": request_id,
123	        "delivery_status": "sent" if success else "failed",
124	    }
125	
126	
127	def complete_recovery(storage: Storage, token: str) -> dict:
128	    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
129	        raise ValidationError("token is required")
130	
131	    request = storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(_hash_token(token))
132	    if request is None:
133	        raise RecoveryError("recovery token is invalid")
134	    if request.used:
135	        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has already been used")
136	    if request.expires_at <= now_iso():
137	        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has expired")
138	
139	    storage.mark_recovery_used(request.request_id)
140	
141	    return {
142	        "status": "completed",
143	        "request_id": request.request_id,
144	        "account_id": request.account_id,
145	        "org_id": request.org_id,
146	    }
147	
148	
149	def retry_notifications(storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
150	    pending = storage.list_pending_recovery_requests()
151	
152	    retried = 0
153	    succeeded = 0
154	    failed = 0
155	
156	    for request in pending:
157	        attempt = storage.latest_failed_attempt(request.request_id)
158	        if attempt is None or attempt.retry_locator is None:
159	            continue
160	
161	        account_id = notice.account_id_from_retry_locator(
162	            attempt.retry_locator, request.account_id
163	        )
164	        try:
165	            account = storage.get_account(account_id)
166	        except NotFoundError:
167	            continue
168	
169	        retried += 1
170	        success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(
171	            mail_endpoint, account.current_email, request.token_plain
172	        )
173	        retry_locator = None
174	        if not success:
175	            retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
176	        storage.record_notification_attempt(
177	            request_id=request.request_id,
178	            account_id=account.account_id,
179	            endpoint=mail_endpoint,
180	            success=success,
181	            receipt=receipt,
182	            retry_locator=retry_locator,
183	        )
184	        if success:
185	            succeeded += 1
186	        else:
187	            failed += 1
188	
189	    return {"retried": retried, "succeeded": succeeded, "failed": failed}

  currently owns it, so notification delivery always resolves the recipient
  from the account's *current* email at send time -- including on retry,
  after `accountsvc.notice` rebuilds the pending delivery's account binding.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import secrets
import uuid

from . import notice
from .errors import NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
from .mailer import send_recovery_mail
from .models import RecoveryRequest, validate_email, validate_id
from .storage import Storage
from .timeutil import future_iso, now_iso

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900


def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def create_account(storage: Storage, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    validate_email(email)
    account = storage.create_account(org_id, account_id, email)
    return account_to_dict(account)


def change_email(storage: Storage, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    validate_email(new_email)
    account = storage.change_email(account_id, new_email)
    return account_to_dict(account)


def show_account(storage: Storage, account_id: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    account = storage.get_account(account_id)
    history = storage.get_email_history(account_id)
    mfa = storage.get_mfa_enrollment(account_id)
    return {
        "account_id": account.account_id,
        "org_id": account.org_id,
        "current_email": account.current_email,
        "created_at": account.created_at,
        "mfa_enrolled": mfa.enrolled,
        "email_history": [
            {
                "email": entry.email,
                "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
                "effective_to": entry.effective_to,
                "released": entry.released,
            }
            for entry in history
        ],
    }


def account_to_dict(account) -> dict:
    return {
        "account_id": account.account_id,
        "org_id": account.org_id,
        "current_email": account.current_email,
        "created_at": account.created_at,
    }


def start_recovery(storage: Storage, org_id: str, email: str, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
    validate_email(email)

    account = storage.find_account_by_current_email(org_id, email)
    if account is None:
        raise NotFoundError(
            f"no account in organization '{org_id}' currently uses email '{email}'"
        )

    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    created_at = now_iso()
    expires_at = future_iso(RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS)

    request = RecoveryRequest(
        request_id=request_id,
        account_id=account.account_id,
        org_id=org_id,
        token_hash=_hash_token(token),
        token_plain=token,
        created_at=created_at,
        expires_at=expires_at,
        used_at=None,
    )
    storage.create_recovery_request(request)

    success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(mail_endpoint, email, token)
    retry_locator = None
    if not success:
        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
    storage.record_notification_attempt(
        request_id=request_id,
        account_id=account.account_id,
        endpoint=mail_endpoint,
        success=success,
        receipt=receipt,
        retry_locator=retry_locator,
    )

    return {
        "request_id": request_id,
        "delivery_status": "sent" if success else "failed",
    }


def complete_recovery(storage: Storage, token: str) -> dict:
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
        raise ValidationError("token is required")

    request = storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(_hash_token(token))
    if request is None:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token is invalid")
    if request.used:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has already been used")
    if request.expires_at <= now_iso():
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has expired")

    storage.mark_recovery_used(request.request_id)

    return {
        "status": "completed",
        "request_id": request.request_id,
        "account_id": request.account_id,
        "org_id": request.org_id,
    }


def retry_notifications(storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
    pending = storage.list_pending_recovery_requests()

    retried = 0
    succeeded = 0
    failed = 0

    for request in pending:
        attempt = storage.latest_failed_attempt(request.request_id)
        if attempt is None or attempt.retry_locator is None:
            continue

        account_id = notice.account_id_from_retry_locator(
            attempt.retry_locator, request.account_id
        )
        try:
            account = storage.get_account(account_id)
        except NotFoundError:
            continue

        retried += 1
        success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(
            mail_endpoint, account.current_email, request.token_plain
        )
        retry_locator = None
        if not success:
            retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
        storage.record_notification_attempt(
            request_id=request.request_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            endpoint=mail_endpoint,
            success=success,
            receipt=receipt,
            retry_locator=retry_locator,
        )
        if success:
            succeeded += 1
        else:
            failed += 1

    return {"retried": retried, "succeeded": succeeded, "failed": failed}

"""Loopback HTTP service exposing the recovery endpoints.

    POST /recovery/start
    POST /recovery/complete
    POST /recovery/notifications/retry   (bearer-authenticated)

Every request body is bounded before it is parsed, and every response is
JSON with sorted keys so output is stable and comparable across processes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple

from . import service
from .errors import AccountSvcError, AuthError, NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
from .storage import Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 65536

_ERROR_STATUS = {
    ValidationError: 400,
    NotFoundError: 404,
    RecoveryError: 400,
    AuthError: 401,
}


class RecoveryHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True

    def __init__(self, address: Tuple[str, int], database_path: str, bearer_token: str, mail_endpoint: str):
        super().__init__(address, RecoveryRequestHandler)
        self.storage = Storage(database_path)
        self.bearer_token = bearer_token
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server: RecoveryHTTPServer

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output clean; audit_events is the durable log

    def _send_json(self, status: int, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _read_json_body(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise ValidationError("Content-Length header is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValidationError("Content-Length must be an integer") from exc
        if length < 0 or length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise ValidationError(f"request body must not exceed {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes")
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            raise ValidationError("request body must be valid JSON") from exc
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise ValidationError("request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def _require_bearer_auth(self) -> None:
        header = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        prefix = "Bearer "
        if not header.startswith(prefix):
            raise AuthError("missing bearer token")
        presented = header[len(prefix):]
        if not hmac.compare_digest(presented, self.server.bearer_token):
            raise AuthError("invalid bearer token")

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        try:
            if self.path == "/recovery/start":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                organization = body.get("organization")
                email = body.get("email")
                if not isinstance(organization, str) or not isinstance(email, str):
                    raise ValidationError("organization and email are required strings")
                result = service.start_recovery(
                    self.server.storage, organization, email, self.server.mail_endpoint
                )
                self._send_json(200, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/complete":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                token = body.get("token")
                if not isinstance(token, str):
                    raise ValidationError("token is required")
                result = service.complete_recovery(self.server.storage, token)
                self._send_json(200, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/notifications/retry":
                self._require_bearer_auth()
                self._read_json_body_optional()
                result = service.retry_notifications(
                    self.server.storage, self.server.mail_endpoint
                )
                self._send_json(200, result)
            else:
                self._send_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
        except AccountSvcError as exc:
            status = _ERROR_STATUS.get(type(exc), 400)
            self._send_json(status, {"error": str(exc)})
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive catch-all
            self._send_json(500, {"error": f"internal error: {exc}"})

    def _read_json_body_optional(self) -> None:
        if self.headers.get("Content-Length"):
            self._read_json_body()


def run_server(database_path: str, bearer_token: str, mail_endpoint: str, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    server = RecoveryHTTPServer((host, port), database_path, bearer_token, mail_endpoint)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()

import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc import service
from accountsvc.httpserver import MAX_BODY_BYTES, RecoveryHTTPServer
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _FakeMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Loopback stand-in for the configured mail provider."""

    fail_first_n = 0
    captured = []

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        type(self).captured.append(json.loads(body))
        if type(self).fail_first_n > 0:
            type(self).fail_first_n -= 1
            self.send_response(503)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"provider unavailable")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"status": "queued"}')


class AdminHttpTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "test-bearer-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")

        handler_cls = type(
            f"MailHandler_{id(self)}", (_FakeMailHandler,), {"fail_first_n": 0, "captured": []}
        )
        self.mail_handler_cls = handler_cls
        self.mail_server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler_cls)
        self.mail_port = self.mail_server.server_address[1]
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()

        self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
            ("127.0.0.1", 0),
            db_path,
            self.BEARER_TOKEN,
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
        )
        self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
        self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.svc_thread.start()

        self.storage = Storage(db_path)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.svc_server.shutdown()
        self.svc_server.server_close()
        self.mail_server.shutdown()
        self.mail_server.server_close()
        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def post(self, path, payload=None, headers=None, raw_body=None):
        data = raw_body if raw_body is not None else json.dumps(payload or {}).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}",
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read())


class RecoveryStartTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_start_returns_request_id_and_status_but_never_the_token(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("request_id", body)
        self.assertIn("delivery_status", body)
        self.assertNotIn("token", body)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", body)

    def test_start_unknown_account_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "nope@b.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_start_missing_fields_is_bad_request(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_start_records_failed_delivery_for_retry(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.mail_handler_cls.fail_first_n = 99
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "failed")


class RecoveryCompleteTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_complete_with_invalid_token_fails(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": "bogus"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_complete_with_missing_token_field_fails(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)


class RetryAuthTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_retry_without_auth_header_is_unauthorized(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/notifications/retry", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_retry_with_wrong_token_is_unauthorized(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": "Bearer wrong-token"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 401)

    def test_retry_with_correct_token_is_authorized(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"retried": 0, "succeeded": 0, "failed": 0})

    def test_retry_resends_same_token_and_uses_current_email(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "old@b.com")
        self.mail_handler_cls.fail_first_n = 1
        start_status, start_body = self.post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "old@b.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(start_body["delivery_status"], "failed")
        first_payload = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[-1]

        # The address only authorizes delivery while currently owned, so a
        # later change must redirect retry to the NEW current email...
        service.change_email(self.storage, "acct1", "new@b.com")

        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body, {"retried": 1, "succeeded": 1, "failed": 0})

        retry_payload = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[-1]
        self.assertEqual(retry_payload["recipient"], "new@b.com")
        # ...while keeping the exact original token bound to the request.
        self.assertEqual(retry_payload["recovery_token"], first_payload["recovery_token"])

    def test_retry_no_op_when_nothing_pending(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["retried"], 0)


class BoundedRequestValidationTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_oversized_body_is_rejected(self):
        oversized = json.dumps(
            {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com", "padding": "x" * (MAX_BODY_BYTES + 1)}
        ).encode("utf-8")
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", raw_body=oversized)
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_non_json_body_is_rejected(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", raw_body=b"not json at all")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_unknown_route_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/unknown", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

4	so that a writer in one process and a reader in another process observe a
5	consistent, durable view of the same state -- this is what lets
6	`show-account` in a fresh process see what `create-account` committed in a
7	prior one.

"""Durable SQLite storage for the account recovery service.

Each call opens and closes its own connection. The database runs in WAL mode
so that a writer in one process and a reader in another process observe a
consistent, durable view of the same state -- this is what lets
`show-account` in a fresh process see what `create-account` committed in a
prior one.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import contextlib
import sqlite3
from typing import Iterator, List, Optional

from .errors import ConflictError, NotFoundError
from .models import (
    Account,
    AuditEvent,
    EmailHistoryEntry,
    MfaEnrollment,
    NotificationAttempt,
    ProviderDeliveryReceipt,
    RecoveryRequest,
)
from .timeutil import now_iso

SCHEMA = """
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS organizations (
    org_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS accounts (
    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations(org_id),
    current_email TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS email_history (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    email TEXT NOT NULL,
    effective_from TEXT NOT NULL,
    effective_to TEXT,
    released INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ux_email_history_current
    ON email_history(org_id, email)
    WHERE effective_to IS NULL;

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_email_history_account
    ON email_history(account_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS mfa_enrollments (
    account_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    method TEXT NOT NULL,
    enrolled INTEGER NOT NULL,
    updated_at TEXT NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS recovery_requests (
    request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES accounts(account_id),
    org_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    token_hash TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    token_plain TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    used_at TEXT
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS notification_attempts (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES recovery_requests(request_id),
    account_id TEXT NOT NULL,
    attempt_number INTEGER NOT NULL,
    sent_at TEXT NOT NULL,
    endpoint TEXT NOT NULL,
    success INTEGER NOT NULL,
    receipt_text TEXT NOT NULL,
    retry_locator TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS ix_notification_attempts_request
    ON notification_attempts(request_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS audit_events (
    id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ts TEXT NOT NULL,
    org_id TEXT,
    account_id TEXT,
    event_type TEXT NOT NULL,
    detail TEXT NOT NULL
);
"""


class Storage:
    """SQLite-backed persistence for organizations, accounts, and recovery."""

    def __init__(self, database_path: str) -> None:
        self.database_path = database_path
        self._init_schema()

    @contextlib.contextmanager
    def _connect(self) -> Iterator[sqlite3.Connection]:
        conn = sqlite3.connect(self.database_path, timeout=30.0, isolation_level=None)
        try:
            conn.execute("PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL")
            conn.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")
            conn.execute("PRAGMA busy_timeout=30000")
            conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
            yield conn
        finally:
            conn.close()

    def _init_schema(self) -> None:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.executescript(SCHEMA)

    # -- audit -----------------------------------------------------------

    def _record_audit(
        self,
        conn: sqlite3.Connection,
        event_type: str,
        detail: str,
        org_id: Optional[str] = None,
        account_id: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        event = AuditEvent(
            event_type=event_type,
            ts=now_iso(),
            detail=detail,
            org_id=org_id,
            account_id=account_id,
        )
        conn.execute(
            "INSERT INTO audit_events (ts, org_id, account_id, event_type, detail) "
            "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
            (event.ts, event.org_id, event.account_id, event.event_type, event.detail),
        )

    def list_audit_events(self) -> List[AuditEvent]:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, ts, org_id, account_id, event_type, detail "
                "FROM audit_events ORDER BY id ASC"
            ).fetchall()
        return [
            AuditEvent(
                event_id=row["id"],
                ts=row["ts"],
                org_id=row["org_id"],
                account_id=row["account_id"],
                event_type=row["event_type"],
                detail=row["detail"],
            )
            for row in rows
        ]

    # -- organizations / accounts -----------------------------------------

    def create_account(self, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> Account:
        created_at = now_iso()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                existing = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT account_id FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?",
                    (account_id,),
                ).fetchone()
                if existing is not None:
                    raise ConflictError(f"account '{account_id}' already exists")

                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO organizations (org_id, created_at) VALUES (?, ?) "
                    "ON CONFLICT(org_id) DO NOTHING",
                    (org_id, created_at),
                )
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO accounts (account_id, org_id, current_email, created_at) "
                    "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (account_id, org_id, email, created_at),
                )
                try:
                    conn.execute(
                        "INSERT INTO email_history "
                        "(account_id, org_id, email, effective_from, effective_to, released) "
                        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, 0)",
                        (account_id, org_id, email, created_at),
                    )
                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"email '{email}' is already in use in organization '{org_id}'"
                    ) from exc
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO mfa_enrollments (account_id, method, enrolled, updated_at) "
                    "VALUES (?, 'none', 0, ?)",
                    (account_id, created_at),
                )
                self._record_audit(
                    conn,
                    "account_created",
                    f"account '{account_id}' created in org '{org_id}' with email '{email}'",
                    org_id=org_id,
                    account_id=account_id,
                )
                conn.execute("COMMIT")
            except Exception:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise
        return Account(
            account_id=account_id, org_id=org_id, current_email=email, created_at=created_at
        )

    def get_account(self, account_id: str) -> Account:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT account_id, org_id, current_email, created_at "
                "FROM accounts WHERE account_id = ?",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"account '{account_id}' not found")
        return Account(
            account_id=row["account_id"],
            org_id=row["org_id"],
            current_email=row["current_email"],
            created_at=row["created_at"],
        )

    def get_email_history(self, account_id: str) -> List[EmailHistoryEntry]:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, account_id, org_id, email, effective_from, effective_to, released "
                "FROM email_history WHERE account_id = ? ORDER BY effective_from ASC, id ASC",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchall()
        return [
            EmailHistoryEntry(
                entry_id=row["id"],
                account_id=row["account_id"],
                org_id=row["org_id"],
                email=row["email"],
                effective_from=row["effective_from"],
                effective_to=row["effective_to"],
                released=bool(row["released"]),
            )
            for row in rows
        ]

    def get_mfa_enrollment(self, account_id: str) -> MfaEnrollment:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT account_id, method, enrolled, updated_at "
                "FROM mfa_enrollments WHERE account_id = ?",
                (account_id,),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise NotFoundError(f"account '{account_id}' not found")
        return MfaEnrollment(
            account_id=row["account_id"],
            method=row["method"],
            enrolled=bool(row["enrolled"]),
            updated_at=row["updated_at"],
        )

    def change_email(self, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> Account:
        changed_at = now_iso()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                row = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT account_id, org_id, current_email FROM accounts "
                    "WHERE account_id = ?",
                    (account_id,),
                ).fetchone()
                if row is None:
                    raise NotFoundError(f"account '{account_id}' not found")
                org_id = row["org_id"]
                old_email = row["current_email"]
                if old_email == new_email:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"account '{account_id}' already uses email '{new_email}'"
                    )

                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE email_history SET effective_to = ?, released = 1 "
                    "WHERE account_id = ? AND effective_to IS NULL",
                    (changed_at, account_id),
                )
                try:
                    conn.execute(
                        "INSERT INTO email_history "
                        "(account_id, org_id, email, effective_from, effective_to, released) "
                        "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, NULL, 0)",
                        (account_id, org_id, new_email, changed_at),
                    )
                except sqlite3.IntegrityError as exc:
                    raise ConflictError(
                        f"email '{new_email}' is already in use in organization '{org_id}'"
                    ) from exc
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE accounts SET current_email = ? WHERE account_id = ?",
                    (new_email, account_id),
                )
                self._record_audit(
                    conn,
                    "email_changed",
                    f"account '{account_id}' email changed from '{old_email}' to '{new_email}'",
                    org_id=org_id,
                    account_id=account_id,
                )
                conn.execute("COMMIT")
            except Exception:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise
        return self.get_account(account_id)

    def find_account_by_current_email(self, org_id: str, email: str) -> Optional[Account]:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT a.account_id, a.org_id, a.current_email, a.created_at "
                "FROM accounts a "
                "JOIN email_history h ON h.account_id = a.account_id AND h.effective_to IS NULL "
                "WHERE h.org_id = ? AND h.email = ?",
                (org_id, email),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return Account(
            account_id=row["account_id"],
            org_id=row["org_id"],
            current_email=row["current_email"],
            created_at=row["created_at"],
        )

    # -- recovery requests --------------------------------------------------

    def create_recovery_request(self, request: RecoveryRequest) -> None:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO recovery_requests "
                    "(request_id, account_id, org_id, token_hash, token_plain, created_at, "
                    " expires_at, used_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (
                        request.request_id,
                        request.account_id,
                        request.org_id,
                        request.token_hash,
                        request.token_plain,
                        request.created_at,
                        request.expires_at,
                        request.used_at,
                    ),
                )
                self._record_audit(
                    conn,
                    "recovery_started",
                    f"recovery request '{request.request_id}' created for account "
                    f"'{request.account_id}'",
                    org_id=request.org_id,
                    account_id=request.account_id,
                )
                conn.execute("COMMIT")
            except Exception:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise

    def get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(self, token_hash: str) -> Optional[RecoveryRequest]:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            row = conn.execute(
                "SELECT request_id, account_id, org_id, token_hash, token_plain, "
                "created_at, expires_at, used_at "
                "FROM recovery_requests WHERE token_hash = ?",
                (token_hash,),
            ).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            return None
        return RecoveryRequest(
            request_id=row["request_id"],
            account_id=row["account_id"],
            org_id=row["org_id"],
            token_hash=row["token_hash"],
            token_plain=row["token_plain"],
            created_at=row["created_at"],
            expires_at=row["expires_at"],
            used_at=row["used_at"],
        )

    def mark_recovery_used(self, request_id: str) -> None:
        used_at = now_iso()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                row = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT account_id, org_id FROM recovery_requests WHERE request_id = ?",
                    (request_id,),
                ).fetchone()
                conn.execute(
                    "UPDATE recovery_requests SET used_at = ? WHERE request_id = ?",
                    (used_at, request_id),
                )
                if row is not None:
                    self._record_audit(
                        conn,
                        "recovery_completed",
                        f"recovery request '{request_id}' completed",
                        org_id=row["org_id"],
                        account_id=row["account_id"],
                    )
                conn.execute("COMMIT")
            except Exception:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise

    def list_pending_recovery_requests(self) -> List[RecoveryRequest]:
        """Requests that are unused, unexpired, and have no successful delivery."""
        now = now_iso()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT r.request_id, r.account_id, r.org_id, r.token_hash, r.token_plain, "
                "       r.created_at, r.expires_at, r.used_at "
                "FROM recovery_requests r "
                "WHERE r.used_at IS NULL AND r.expires_at > ? "
                "AND NOT EXISTS ("
                "   SELECT 1 FROM notification_attempts n "
                "   WHERE n.request_id = r.request_id AND n.success = 1"
                ")",
                (now,),
            ).fetchall()
        return [
            RecoveryRequest(
                request_id=row["request_id"],
                account_id=row["account_id"],
                org_id=row["org_id"],
                token_hash=row["token_hash"],
                token_plain=row["token_plain"],
                created_at=row["created_at"],
                expires_at=row["expires_at"],
                used_at=row["used_at"],
            )
            for row in rows
        ]

    # -- notification attempts ----------------------------------------------

    def record_notification_attempt(
        self,
        request_id: str,
        account_id: str,
        endpoint: str,
        success: bool,
        receipt: ProviderDeliveryReceipt,
        retry_locator: Optional[str],
    ) -> NotificationAttempt:
        sent_at = now_iso()
        with self._connect() as conn:
            conn.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
            try:
                prior = conn.execute(
                    "SELECT COALESCE(MAX(attempt_number), 0) AS n "
                    "FROM notification_attempts WHERE request_id = ?",
                    (request_id,),
                ).fetchone()
                attempt_number = int(prior["n"]) + 1
                cur = conn.execute(
                    "INSERT INTO notification_attempts "
                    "(request_id, account_id, attempt_number, sent_at, endpoint, success, "
                    " receipt_text, retry_locator) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",
                    (
                        request_id,
                        account_id,
                        attempt_number,
                        sent_at,
                        endpoint,
                        1 if success else 0,
                        receipt.raw_text,
                        retry_locator,
                    ),
                )
                self._record_audit(
                    conn,
                    "notification_attempt",
                    f"attempt {attempt_number} for request '{request_id}' "
                    f"{'succeeded' if success else 'failed'}",
                    account_id=account_id,
                )
                conn.execute("COMMIT")
            except Exception:
                conn.execute("ROLLBACK")
                raise
        return NotificationAttempt(
            attempt_id=cur.lastrowid,
            request_id=request_id,

            endpoint=endpoint,
            success=success,
            receipt=receipt,
            retry_locator=retry_locator,
        )

    def list_notification_attempts(self, request_id: str) -> List[NotificationAttempt]:
        with self._connect() as conn:
            rows = conn.execute(
                "SELECT id, request_id, account_id, attempt_number, sent_at, endpoint, "
                "success, receipt_text, retry_locator "
                "FROM notification_attempts WHERE request_id = ? ORDER BY attempt_number ASC",
                (request_id,),
            ).fetchall()

            NotificationAttempt(
                attempt_id=row["id"],
                request_id=row["request_id"],
                account_id=row["account_id"],

"""Argument parsing for the accountsvc CLI, kept separate for direct testing.

Preserves the documented CLI shapes:

    create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
    change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
    show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
    serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from typing import List, Optional


def build_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="python -m accountsvc.cli")
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="command", required=True)

    create_account = subparsers.add_parser(

"""Command-line entry point.

    python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
    python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL

Every successful command prints one JSON object with sorted keys to stdout,
so separate invocations -- even from separate processes -- produce
byte-identical output for the same durable state.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from typing import List, Optional

from . import service
from .errors import AccountSvcError
from .httpserver import run_server
from .parser import parse_args
from .storage import Storage


def main(argv: Optional[List[str]] = None) -> int:
    args = parse_args(argv)

    if args.command == "serve":
        run_server(
            database_path=args.database,
            bearer_token=args.bearer_token,
            mail_endpoint=args.mail_endpoint,
            host=args.host,
            port=args.port,
        )
        return 0

    storage = Storage(args.database)
    try:
        if args.command == "create-account":
            result = service.create_account(storage, args.org_id, args.account_id, args.email)
        elif args.command == "change-email":
            result = service.change_email(storage, args.account_id, args.new_email)
        elif args.command == "show-account":
            result = service.show_account(storage, args.account_id)
        else:  # pragma: no cover - argparse guarantees a known command
            raise AccountSvcError(f"unknown command '{args.command}'")
    except AccountSvcError as exc:
        print(json.dumps({"error": str(exc)}, sort_keys=True), file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    print(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

        self.assertEqual(len(history), 1)
        self.assertIsNone(history[0].effective_to)
        self.assertFalse(history[0].released)

    def setUp(self):

        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def _run_cli(self, *args):
        completed = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", *args, "--database", self.db_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
        )
        return completed

    def test_create_in_one_process_visible_in_another(self):
        created = self._run_cli("create-account", "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.assertEqual(created.returncode, 0, created.stderr)

        shown_first = self._run_cli("show-account", "acct1")
        shown_second = self._run_cli("show-account", "acct1")
        self.assertEqual(shown_first.returncode, 0, shown_first.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(shown_second.returncode, 0, shown_second.stderr)

        # Every process is a fresh interpreter with its own sqlite handle:
        # identical stdout bytes prove durable, stably-ordered JSON reads.
        self.assertEqual(shown_first.stdout, shown_second.stdout)

        payload = json.loads(shown_first.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "acct1")
        self.assertEqual(payload["current_email"], "a@b.com")
        # sort_keys=True output has a deterministic key order we can assert on.
        self.assertEqual(
            list(json.loads(shown_first.stdout).keys()),
            sorted(json.loads(shown_first.stdout).keys()),
        )

    def test_change_email_in_one_process_visible_in_another(self):
        self._run_cli("create-account", "org1", "acct1", "old@b.com")
        changed = self._run_cli("change-email", "acct1", "new@b.com")
        self.assertEqual(changed.returncode, 0, changed.stderr)

        payload = json.loads(shown.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["current_email"], "new@b.com")

        result = self._run_cli("show-account", "nope")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        error = json.loads(result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("error", error)

"""Business logic tying storage, models, and mail delivery together.

This module implements the documented behaviors:

* Recovery tokens are secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one
  account and organization at creation time. Email lookup happens only at
  recovery start; a later email change never changes which account a token
  recovers.
* An address only authorizes recovery-link delivery while an account
  currently owns it, so notification delivery always resolves the recipient
  from the account's *current* email at send time -- including on retry,
  after `accountsvc.notice` rebuilds the pending delivery's account binding.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import secrets
import uuid

from . import notice
from .errors import NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
from .mailer import send_recovery_mail
from .models import RecoveryRequest, validate_email, validate_id
from .storage import Storage
from .timeutil import future_iso, now_iso

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900


def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def create_account(storage: Storage, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    validate_email(email)
    account = storage.create_account(org_id, account_id, email)
    return account_to_dict(account)


def change_email(storage: Storage, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    validate_email(new_email)
    account = storage.change_email(account_id, new_email)
    return account_to_dict(account)


def show_account(storage: Storage, account_id: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    account = storage.get_account(account_id)
    history = storage.get_email_history(account_id)
    mfa = storage.get_mfa_enrollment(account_id)
    return {
        "account_id": account.account_id,
        "org_id": account.org_id,
        "current_email": account.current_email,
        "created_at": account.created_at,
        "mfa_enrolled": mfa.enrolled,
        "email_history": [
            {
                "email": entry.email,
                "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
                "effective_to": entry.effective_to,
                "released": entry.released,
            }
            for entry in history
        ],
    }


def account_to_dict(account) -> dict:
    return {
        "account_id": account.account_id,
        "org_id": account.org_id,
        "current_email": account.current_email,
        "created_at": account.created_at,
    }


def start_recovery(storage: Storage, org_id: str, email: str, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
    validate_email(email)

    account = storage.find_account_by_current_email(org_id, email)
    if account is None:
        raise NotFoundError(
            f"no account in organization '{org_id}' currently uses email '{email}'"
        )

    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    created_at = now_iso()
    expires_at = future_iso(RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS)

    request = RecoveryRequest(
        request_id=request_id,
        account_id=account.account_id,
        org_id=org_id,
        token_hash=_hash_token(token),
        token_plain=token,
        created_at=created_at,
        expires_at=expires_at,
        used_at=None,
    )
    storage.create_recovery_request(request)

    success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(mail_endpoint, email, token)
    retry_locator = None
    if not success:
        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
    storage.record_notification_attempt(
        request_id=request_id,
        account_id=account.account_id,
        endpoint=mail_endpoint,
        success=success,
        receipt=receipt,
        retry_locator=retry_locator,
    )

    return {
        "request_id": request_id,
        "delivery_status": "sent" if success else "failed",
    }


def complete_recovery(storage: Storage, token: str) -> dict:
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
        raise ValidationError("token is required")

    request = storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(_hash_token(token))
    if request is None:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token is invalid")
    if request.used:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has already been used")
    if request.expires_at <= now_iso():
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has expired")

    storage.mark_recovery_used(request.request_id)

    return {
        "status": "completed",
        "request_id": request.request_id,
        "account_id": request.account_id,
        "org_id": request.org_id,
    }


def retry_notifications(storage: Storage, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
    pending = storage.list_pending_recovery_requests()

    retried = 0
    succeeded = 0
    failed = 0

    for request in pending:
        attempt = storage.latest_failed_attempt(request.request_id)
        if attempt is None or attempt.retry_locator is None:
            continue

        account_id = notice.account_id_from_retry_locator(
            attempt.retry_locator, request.account_id
        )
        try:
            account = storage.get_account(account_id)
        except NotFoundError:
            continue

        retried += 1
        success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(
            mail_endpoint, account.current_email, request.token_plain
        )
        retry_locator = None
        if not success:
            retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
        storage.record_notification_attempt(
            request_id=request.request_id,
            account_id=account.account_id,
            endpoint=mail_endpoint,
            success=success,
            receipt=receipt,
            retry_locator=retry_locator,
        )
        if success:
            succeeded += 1
        else:
            failed += 1

    return {"retried": retried, "succeeded": succeeded, "failed": failed}

    POST /recovery/complete

from __future__ import annotations

import hmac
import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple

from . import service
from .errors import AccountSvcError, AuthError, NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
from .storage import Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 65536

_ERROR_STATUS = {
    ValidationError: 400,
    NotFoundError: 404,
    RecoveryError: 400,
    AuthError: 401,
}


class RecoveryHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True

    def __init__(self, address: Tuple[str, int], database_path: str, bearer_token: str, mail_endpoint: str):
        super().__init__(address, RecoveryRequestHandler)
        self.storage = Storage(database_path)
        self.bearer_token = bearer_token
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server: RecoveryHTTPServer

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output clean; audit_events is the durable log

    def _send_json(self, status: int, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _read_json_body(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise ValidationError("Content-Length header is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValidationError("Content-Length must be an integer") from exc
        if length < 0 or length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise ValidationError(f"request body must not exceed {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes")
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            raise ValidationError("request body must be valid JSON") from exc
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise ValidationError("request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def _require_bearer_auth(self) -> None:
        header = self.headers.get("Authorization", "")
        prefix = "Bearer "
        if not header.startswith(prefix):
            raise AuthError("missing bearer token")
        presented = header[len(prefix):]

class _FakeMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Loopback stand-in for the configured mail provider."""

    fail_first_n = 0
    captured = []

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        type(self).captured.append(json.loads(body))
        if type(self).fail_first_n > 0:
            type(self).fail_first_n -= 1
            self.send_response(503)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"provider unavailable")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"status": "queued"}')

from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc import notice, service
from accountsvc.httpserver import MAX_BODY_BYTES, RecoveryHTTPServer
from accountsvc.models import RecoveryRequest
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _FakeMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Loopback stand-in for the configured mail provider."""

    fail_first_n = 0
    captured = []

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        type(self).captured.append(json.loads(body))
        if type(self).fail_first_n > 0:
            type(self).fail_first_n -= 1
            self.send_response(503)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"provider unavailable")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"status": "queued"}')


class AdminHttpTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "test-bearer-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")

        handler_cls = type(
            f"MailHandler_{id(self)}", (_FakeMailHandler,), {"fail_first_n": 0, "captured": []}
        )
        self.mail_handler_cls = handler_cls
        self.mail_server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler_cls)
        self.mail_port = self.mail_server.server_address[1]
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()

        self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
            ("127.0.0.1", 0),
            db_path,
            self.BEARER_TOKEN,
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
        )
        self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
        self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.svc_thread.start()

        self.storage = Storage(db_path)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.svc_server.shutdown()
        self.svc_server.server_close()
        self.mail_server.shutdown()
        self.mail_server.server_close()
        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def post(self, path, payload=None, headers=None, raw_body=None):
        data = raw_body if raw_body is not None else json.dumps(payload or {}).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}",
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read())


class RecoveryStartTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_start_returns_request_id_and_status_but_never_the_token(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("request_id", body)
        self.assertIn("delivery_status", body)
        self.assertNotIn("token", body)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", body)

    def test_start_delivers_to_the_accounts_current_email(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "current@b.com")
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "current@b.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "sent")

        self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_handler_cls.captured), 1)
        payload = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[0]
        self.assertEqual(payload["recipient"], "current@b.com")
        self.assertIn("recovery_token", payload)
        # The token that unlocks recovery is only ever sent to the mail
        # provider, never echoed back over HTTP.
        self.assertNotEqual(payload["recovery_token"], "")

    def test_start_unknown_account_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "nope@b.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_start_missing_fields_is_bad_request(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_start_retains_receipt_and_locator_on_failed_delivery(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.mail_handler_cls.fail_first_n = 99
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "failed")

        attempts = self.storage.list_notification_attempts(body["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        attempt = attempts[0]
        self.assertFalse(attempt.success)
        # The provider's opaque response is retained verbatim...
        self.assertEqual(attempt.receipt.raw_text, "provider unavailable")
        # ...alongside the request's trusted account binding, saved through
        # the starter's own locator helper -- not re-derived by this test.
        self.assertEqual(
            attempt.retry_locator,
            notice.encode_retry_locator(attempt.receipt.raw_text, "acct1"),
        )


class RecoveryCompleteTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_complete_with_invalid_token_fails(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": "bogus"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_complete_with_missing_token_field_fails(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_complete_with_the_mailed_token_succeeds(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        token = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[-1]["recovery_token"]

        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(
            body,
            {
                "status": "completed",
                "request_id": body["request_id"],
                "account_id": "acct1",
                "org_id": "org1",
            },
        )

    def test_completed_token_cannot_be_replayed(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        token = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[-1]["recovery_token"]

        first_status, _ = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": token})
        self.assertEqual(first_status, 200)

        second_status, second_body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": token})
        self.assertEqual(second_status, 400)
        self.assertIn("already been used", second_body["error"])

    def test_expired_token_is_rejected(self):
        from accountsvc.models import RecoveryRequest

        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        expired_token = "z" * 32
        request = RecoveryRequest(
            request_id="expired-request",
            account_id="acct1",
            org_id="org1",
            token_hash=hashlib.sha256(expired_token.encode()).hexdigest(),
            token_plain=expired_token,
            created_at="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
            expires_at="2000-01-01T00:15:00+00:00",
        )
        self.storage.create_recovery_request(request)

        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": expired_token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("expired", body["error"])


class RetryRouteNotYetAvailableTests(AdminHttpTestCase):

    then, so the route simply is not registered yet.
    """

    def test_retry_route_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
