# Operator Support Cases — Compatibility Evidence

Scope of this review: `maintenance/inputs/operator-support/` (8 files), covering
compatibility evidence for operator support cases in restart-safe account
recovery retries.

## Method

Each source file was read in full. File type, line count, and SHA-256 checksum
were confirmed with separate, ordinary read-only commands (`file`, `wc -l`,
`shasum -a 256`) run individually per file, not chained. Case counts,
status-value distributions, and platform-value distributions were extracted
per file with format-aware `grep`/`awk` field extraction (matching each
format's own field labels/columns) to avoid over-counting from boilerplate
text. A failure-marker search (`fail`, `error`, `exception`, `timeout`,
`crash`, case-insensitive) was run once per file, separately.

## Evidence table

| Source filename | Type (per `file`) | Lines (`wc -l`) | Data rows | SHA-256 (prefix) | Status counts | Platform counts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `attempt-willow-gate.md` | ASCII text, very long lines | 95 | 91 | `224769d73d7c877f3c19` | compatible 22 / documented 23 / follow-up 23 / review 23 | freebsd-x86_64 23 / linux-x86_64 23 / macos-arm64 22 / windows-x86_64 23 |
| `delivery-granite-bay.log` | ASCII text, very long lines | 96 | 95 | `394e842f8937495b4346` | compatible 23 / documented 24 / follow-up 24 / review 24 | freebsd-x86_64 24 / linux-x86_64 24 / macos-arm64 23 / windows-x86_64 24 |
| `identity-north-star.csv` | CSV text | 103 | 102 | `a75869681dc92fe3cdda` | compatible 25 / documented 26 / follow-up 25 / review 26 | freebsd-x86_64 25 / linux-x86_64 26 / macos-arm64 25 / windows-x86_64 26 |
| `mailbox-blue-harbor.md` | ASCII text, very long lines | 95 | 91 | `9a73b909cf9fb8609d36` | compatible 22 / documented 23 / follow-up 23 / review 23 | freebsd-x86_64 23 / linux-x86_64 23 / macos-arm64 22 / windows-x86_64 23 |
| `request-cedar-lane.log` | ASCII text, very long lines | 97 | 96 | `69964c9ba7ee0c97a5d0` | compatible 24 / documented 24 / follow-up 24 / review 24 | freebsd-x86_64 24 / linux-x86_64 24 / macos-arm64 24 / windows-x86_64 24 |
| `restart-quiet-river.jsonl` | JSON data | 89 | 89 | `32bab1f9ee841dad2b56` | compatible 22 / documented 22 / follow-up 22 / review 23 | freebsd-x86_64 22 / linux-x86_64 23 / macos-arm64 22 / windows-x86_64 22 |
| `tenant-silver-pine.yaml` | ASCII text, very long lines | 93 | 92 | `9398cd7c6054d77db851` | compatible 23 / documented 23 / follow-up 23 / review 23 | freebsd-x86_64 23 / linux-x86_64 23 / macos-arm64 23 / windows-x86_64 23 |
| `token-amber-field.csv` | CSV text | 104 | 103 | `7b909b510bd42ddf98e1` | compatible 25 / documented 26 / follow-up 26 / review 26 | freebsd-x86_64 26 / linux-x86_64 26 / macos-arm64 25 / windows-x86_64 26 |

("Data rows" is total lines minus header/title lines, confirmed per file:
`.md` files carry a 4-line preamble before the first case entry; `.log` files
carry a 1-line title comment; `.csv` files carry a 1-line column header;
`.yaml` carries a 1-line title comment; `.jsonl` has no header line.)

## Cases and structure

- Every row in every file follows the same `row mod 4` cycle across both
  status (`review`, `documented`, `follow-up`, `compatible`) and platform
  (`linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`, `freebsd-x86_64`, `macos-arm64`), in that
  fixed order, starting from row 1 in each file.
- Case identifiers are self-referential: each row's case ID embeds its own
  source filename and row number (e.g. `attempt-willow-gate.md case 1`,
  `case=delivery-granite-bay.log:1`, `"identity-north-star.csv:1"`,
  `tenant-silver-pine.yaml:1`, `restart-quiet-river.jsonl:1`).
- Every row's note text follows an identical boilerplate template across all
  8 files: "Recorded restart-safe account recovery retries evidence for
  operator support cases. The archived evidence marks this case as {status}
  on {platform}. The review records stated inputs, observed output, operator
  note, and compatibility limit." The word "archived" appears in this
  template in every row of every file, even though only two of the eight
  titles use the word "archived" (see below) — the source files do not state
  why "archived" appears in the note text of files whose own titles do not
  describe the evidence as archived.
- Title/heading text differs by file and does not fully align with file type:
  - `attempt-willow-gate.md` and `mailbox-blue-harbor.md`: `# Operator
    Support Cases` / `Scope: restart-safe account recovery retries.`
    (identical heading text in both files).
  - `delivery-granite-bay.log` and `request-cedar-lane.log`: `# archived
    operator support cases for restart-safe account recovery retries`
    (identical heading text in both files; only these two files' titles use
    "archived").
  - `tenant-silver-pine.yaml`: `# restart-safe account recovery retries:
    operator support cases` (no "archived" in the title).
  - `identity-north-star.csv`, `token-amber-field.csv`,
    `restart-quiet-river.jsonl`: no title/heading line; each starts directly
    with a header row (CSV) or the first case record (JSONL).

## Failure and platform-marker search

A case-insensitive search for `fail`, `error`, `exception`, `timeout`, and
`crash` across all 8 files returned no matches. Status values found are
limited to `review`, `documented`, `follow-up`, and `compatible`; platform
values found are limited to `linux-x86_64`, `windows-x86_64`,
`freebsd-x86_64`, and `macos-arm64`. The sources do not record any failure,
error, exception, timeout, or crash cases.

## Open questions

- **File-type pairing is inconsistent across formats.** The two `.md` files
  match exactly in data-row count (91 and 91). The two `.log` files do not
  match (95 vs. 96). The two `.csv` files do not match (102 vs. 103). The
  single `.yaml` file (92 rows) and single `.jsonl` file (89 rows) have no
  same-format counterpart in this directory at all. The sources do not state
  whether this directory was meant to hold matched format pairs (as with
  prior reviewed directories) or why three of the four possible pairings
  (`.log`, `.csv`, and the missing `.yaml`/`.jsonl` partners) diverge from
  the one pairing that does match (`.md`).
- **The "archived" wording in the shared note template is unexplained.**
  Every row's note text says "The archived evidence marks this case as...",
  regardless of whether the file's own title mentions "archived." The
  sources do not state what makes this evidence "archived" or how that
  relates to the file's own (non-)use of the word in its title.
- **No stated relationship between "operator support cases" and the
  "archived environment results" / "restart results" evidence reviewed
  previously.** Note text, boilerplate phrasing, and self-referential case
  ID structure are consistent with the patterns documented in
  `maintenance/reports/environment-findings.md`, but no source file in
  either review states whether these are the same underlying evidence,
  sequential snapshots, or unrelated collections.
- **No stated follow-up ownership.** Rows marked `status: follow-up` and
  `status: review` appear throughout every file, but no source states who is
  responsible for acting on them or by when.
- **Continuation of the "disappearing input directory" pattern.** As of this
  review, `ls -la maintenance/inputs/` shows only `operator-support/`
  present — the `environment-results/` and `restart-results/` directories
  reviewed in earlier maintenance passes are both no longer present on disk,
  and the `current-fixtures/`/`legacy-fixtures/` directories from the
  earliest reviews are also absent. This is the fourth consecutive
  maintenance-input directory to disappear after being reviewed; the sources
  do not explain why.

## Handoff note

`maintenance/inputs/operator-support/` contains 8 read-only evidence files
(2 Markdown, 2 log, 2 CSV, 1 YAML, 1 JSONL) describing operator support cases
for restart-safe account recovery retries, cycling deterministically through
4 status values and 4 platform values with no failure/error markers present
anywhere in the set. Before treating this evidence as reconciled, the next
reviewer should decide: (1) whether the `.log`/`.csv` row-count mismatches
and the unpaired `.yaml`/`.jsonl` files are data entry issues or intentional;
(2) whether "operator support cases" is the same evidence as, or a different
population from, the "archived environment results" and "restart results"
sets already reviewed in `environment-findings.md`; and (3) whether the
repeated disappearance of each reviewed input directory reflects an
intentional cleanup process this review has no visibility into. This
maintenance work is kept separate from `accountsvc` product code and product
tests; no files outside `maintenance/` were read or modified for this review.

content.content:
# Account Recovery Service starter

This disposable starter grows into a local account and MFA recovery service.
Use only the Python standard library.

Keep these CLI shapes stable:

```text
python -m accountsvc.cli create-account ORG_ID ACCOUNT_ID EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli change-email ACCOUNT_ID NEW_EMAIL --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli show-account ACCOUNT_ID --database STATE.db
python -m accountsvc.cli serve --database STATE.db --bearer-token TOKEN --mail-endpoint URL
```

The loopback HTTP service exposes `POST /recovery/start`,
`POST /recovery/complete`, and authenticated
`POST /recovery/notifications/retry`. Recovery start accepts an organization
and current email address as `organization` and `email`. Recovery completion
accepts `token`. Start returns a request id and delivery status, not the secret
recovery token.

The service sends each recovery link to the configured loopback mail endpoint
as JSON with `recipient` and `recovery_token`. A non-success response leaves a
durable notification for later retry. Failed provider responses keep a recovery
locator in `accountsvc.notice`. `encode_retry_locator` creates it, and
`account_id_from_retry_locator` resolves the account when retry rebuilds the
pending delivery.

A recovery token is secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one account
and organization when the service creates it. Email lookup selects the account
only at recovery start. A later email change never changes which account the
token can recover.

An account may release an old email address during an explicit change. Another
account in the same organization may then claim it. An address authorizes
recovery-link delivery only while the account currently owns it. Email history
is useful for support and audit, but it is never account identity.

The initial scaffold contains only this contract. Build the parser, storage,
account administration, recovery flow, notification delivery, loopback HTTP
service, and tests.

import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc import notice, service
from accountsvc.httpserver import MAX_BODY_BYTES, RecoveryHTTPServer
from accountsvc.models import RecoveryRequest
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _FakeMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Loopback stand-in for the configured mail provider."""

    fail_first_n = 0
    captured = []

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        type(self).captured.append(json.loads(body))
        if type(self).fail_first_n > 0:
            type(self).fail_first_n -= 1
            self.send_response(503)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"provider unavailable")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"status": "queued"}')


class AdminHttpTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "test-bearer-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")

        handler_cls = type(
            f"MailHandler_{id(self)}", (_FakeMailHandler,), {"fail_first_n": 0, "captured": []}
        )
        self.mail_handler_cls = handler_cls
        self.mail_server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler_cls)
        self.mail_port = self.mail_server.server_address[1]
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()

        self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
            ("127.0.0.1", 0),
            db_path,
            self.BEARER_TOKEN,
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
        )
        self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
        self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.svc_thread.start()

        self.storage = Storage(db_path)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.svc_server.shutdown()
        self.svc_server.server_close()
        self.mail_server.shutdown()
        self.mail_server.server_close()
        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def post(self, path, payload=None, headers=None, raw_body=None):
        data = raw_body if raw_body is not None else json.dumps(payload or {}).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}",
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read())


class RecoveryStartTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_start_returns_request_id_and_status_but_never_the_token(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("request_id", body)
        self.assertIn("delivery_status", body)
        self.assertNotIn("token", body)

class SeparateProcessStableJsonTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Prove durable state is visible, with stable JSON, across processes."""

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")

    def tearDown(self):
        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def _run_cli(self, *args):
        completed = subprocess.run(
            [sys.executable, "-m", "accountsvc.cli", *args, "--database", self.db_path],
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            cwd=os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
        )
        return completed

    def test_create_in_one_process_visible_in_another(self):
        created = self._run_cli("create-account", "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.assertEqual(created.returncode, 0, created.stderr)

        shown_first = self._run_cli("show-account", "acct1")
        shown_second = self._run_cli("show-account", "acct1")
        self.assertEqual(shown_first.returncode, 0, shown_first.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(shown_second.returncode, 0, shown_second.stderr)

        # Every process is a fresh interpreter with its own sqlite handle:
        # identical stdout bytes prove durable, stably-ordered JSON reads.
        self.assertEqual(shown_first.stdout, shown_second.stdout)

        payload = json.loads(shown_first.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["account_id"], "acct1")
        self.assertEqual(payload["current_email"], "a@b.com")
        # sort_keys=True output has a deterministic key order we can assert on.
        self.assertEqual(
            list(json.loads(shown_first.stdout).keys()),
            sorted(json.loads(shown_first.stdout).keys()),
        )

    def test_change_email_in_one_process_visible_in_another(self):
        self._run_cli("create-account", "org1", "acct1", "old@b.com")
        changed = self._run_cli("change-email", "acct1", "new@b.com")
        self.assertEqual(changed.returncode, 0, changed.stderr)

        shown = self._run_cli("show-account", "acct1")
        payload = json.loads(shown.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(payload["current_email"], "new@b.com")

    def test_show_missing_account_fails_cleanly(self):
        result = self._run_cli("show-account", "nope")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        error = json.loads(result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("error", error)


if __name__ == "__main__":

# Contributor Testing Guide

How to run this repository's tests, and the conventions the existing test
suite follows for temporary databases and loopback HTTP servers. Reflects
what [`tests/`](../tests/) actually does, not aspirational practice.

## Running the test suite

Run everything (`accountsvc` tests and the isolated `devtools` test) with
`unittest`'s discovery mode from the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Add `-v` for per-test output:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Run a single test module by its dotted path, e.g. only the storage tests:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests.test_storage -v
```

The suite is split across these modules in [`tests/`](../tests/):

| Module | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`tests/test_parser.py`](../tests/test_parser.py) | `argparse` definitions in [`accountsvc/parser.py`](../accountsvc/parser.py). |
| [`tests/test_models.py`](../tests/test_models.py) | Data classes and field validation in [`accountsvc/models.py`](../accountsvc/models.py). |
| [`tests/test_notice.py`](../tests/test_notice.py) | Retry-locator encode/decode helpers in [`accountsvc/notice.py`](../accountsvc/notice.py). |
| [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) | SQLite-backed storage, the service layer, and cross-process durability. |
| [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py) | The loopback HTTP service end to end. |
| [`tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py`](../tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py) | The standalone `devtools.sqlite_summary` tool (see below). |

No third-party test runner or plugin is required — everything here uses only
the standard library's `unittest`.

## Temporary-database handling

Tests that need a database never touch a shared or checked-in file. Each
test case creates its own `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` in `setUp` and
builds a database path inside it, then cleans it up in `tearDown`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    self.db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")
    self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)

def tearDown(self):
    self._tmpdir.cleanup()
```

This pattern appears in [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py)
and [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py). Every test gets a fresh,
isolated SQLite file, so tests can run in any order without sharing state.

[`accountsvc/storage.py`](../accountsvc/storage.py) opens the database with
`isolation_level=None` and sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, and each call opens
and closes its own connection rather than holding one open for the object's
lifetime.

`SeparateProcessStableJsonTests` in
[`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) goes a step further: it
points two separate `python -m accountsvc.cli ...` subprocess invocations at
the same temporary database path to prove that state written by one process
is durably visible, with stably-ordered JSON, to another:

```bash
python3 -m accountsvc.cli create-account org1 acct1 a@b.com --database STATE.db
python3 -m accountsvc.cli show-account acct1 --database STATE.db
```

## Loopback test conventions

The HTTP tests never bind a fixed port. They bind to `("127.0.0.1", 0)` and
let the OS choose a free ephemeral port, then read the actual port back off
`server_address[1]`:

```python
self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
    ("127.0.0.1", 0),
    db_path,
    self.BEARER_TOKEN,
    f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
)
self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
```

Each server runs in a background daemon thread so the test body can make
requests against it directly:

```python
self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
self.svc_thread.start()
```

`tearDown` always calls `shutdown()` followed by `server_close()` on every
server started in `setUp`, so no listening socket outlives a test.

To exercise recovery-link delivery without a real mail provider,
[`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) and
[`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py) stand up a second loopback
server — a small `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` subclass acting as a fake mail
endpoint — the same way, and point the service's `--mail-endpoint` at it.
Tests against the recovery service itself issue plain `urllib.request` calls
against `http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}`.

See [`accountsvc/httpserver.py`](../accountsvc/httpserver.py) for the
`RecoveryHTTPServer` being exercised this way.

## Isolated `devtools` tests

[`devtools/sqlite_summary.py`](../devtools/sqlite_summary.py) is a
standalone, read-only, standard-library-only command that reports SQLite
table names and row counts as JSON. It is deliberately isolated from the
`accountsvc` package: it never imports `accountsvc`, and
[`tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py`](../tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py)
imports only from `devtools.sqlite_summary`, not from `accountsvc`.

Like the `accountsvc` tests, each `devtools` test case gets its own
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` fixture. Coverage includes a database with
no tables (a valid, non-malformed empty database) and a file that is not a
SQLite database at all, to confirm both are handled distinctly:

```python
def test_empty_database_reports_no_tables(self):
    ...
    self.assertEqual(summarize(path), {})

def test_malformed_file_is_rejected(self):
    ...
    with self.assertRaises(SqliteSummaryError):
        summarize(path)
```

CLI-level behavior (`main()`) is tested by capturing stdout/stderr with
`contextlib.redirect_stdout` / `contextlib.redirect_stderr` rather than
spawning a subprocess.

Run just this module:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests.test_devtools_sqlite_summary -v
```

Or run the tool directly against a database file:

```bash
python3 -m devtools.sqlite_summary STATE.db
```

       # Contributor Testing Guide

       How to run this repository's tests, and the conventions the existing test
       suite follows for temporary databases and loopback HTTP servers. Reflects
       what [`tests/`](../tests/) actually does, not aspirational practice.

       ## Running the test suite

       Run everything (`accountsvc` tests and the isolated `devtools` test) with
       `unittest`'s discovery mode from the repository root:

       ```bash
       python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
       ```

       Add `-v` for per-test output:

       ```bash
       python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
       ```

       Run a single test module by its dotted path, e.g. only the storage tests:

       ```bash
       python3 -m unittest tests.test_storage -v
       ```

       The suite is split across these modules in [`tests/`](../tests/):

       | Module | Covers |
       |---|---|
       | [`tests/test_parser.py`](../tests/test_parser.py) | `argparse` definitions in [`accountsvc/parser.py`](../accountsvc/parser.py). |
       | [`tests/test_models.py`](../tests/test_models.py) | Data classes and field validation in [`accountsvc/models.py`](../accountsvc/models.py). |
       | [`tests/test_notice.py`](../tests/test_notice.py) | Retry-locator encode/decode helpers in [`accountsvc/notice.py`](../accountsvc/notice.py). |
       | [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) | SQLite-backed storage, the service layer, and cross-process durability. |
       | [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py) | The loopback HTTP service end to end. |
       | [`tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py`](../tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py) | The standalone `devtools.sqlite_summary` tool (see below). |

       No third-party test runner or plugin is required — everything here uses only
       the standard library's `unittest`.

       ## Temporary-database handling

       Tests that need a database never touch a shared or checked-in file. Each
       test case creates its own `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` in `setUp` and
       builds a database path inside it, then cleans it up in `tearDown`:

       ```python
       def setUp(self):
           self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
           self.db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")
           self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)

       def tearDown(self):
           self._tmpdir.cleanup()
       ```

       This pattern appears in [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py)
       and [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py). Every test gets a fresh,
       isolated SQLite file, so tests can run in any order without sharing state.

       [`accountsvc/storage.py`](../accountsvc/storage.py) opens the database with
       `isolation_level=None` and sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, and each call opens
       and closes its own connection rather than holding one open for the object's
       lifetime.

       the same temporary database path to prove that state written by one process
       is durably visible, with stably-ordered JSON, to another:

       ```bash
       python3 -m accountsvc.cli create-account org1 acct1 a@b.com --database STATE.db
       python3 -m accountsvc.cli show-account acct1 --database STATE.db
       ```

       ## Loopback test conventions

       The HTTP tests never bind a fixed port. They bind to `("127.0.0.1", 0)` and
       let the OS choose a free ephemeral port, then read the actual port back off
       `server_address[1]`:

```python
       self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
           ("127.0.0.1", 0),
           db_path,
           self.BEARER_TOKEN,
           f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
       )
       self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
       ```

       Each server runs in a background daemon thread so the test body can make
       requests against it directly:

```python
       self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
       self.svc_thread.start()
       ```

       `tearDown` always calls `shutdown()` followed by `server_close()` on every
       server started in `setUp`, so no listening socket outlives a test.

       [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) and
       [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py) stand up a second loopback
       server — a small `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` subclass acting as a fake mail
       endpoint — the same way, and point the service's `--mail-endpoint` at it.

       against `http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}`.

       `RecoveryHTTPServer` being exercised this way.

       table names and row counts as JSON. It is deliberately isolated from the


       Or run the tool directly against a database file:

       ```bash

       ```

# Contributor Testing Guide

How to run this repository's tests, and the conventions the existing test
suite follows for temporary databases and loopback HTTP servers. Reflects
what [`tests/`](../tests/) actually does, not aspirational practice.

## Running the test suite

Run everything (`accountsvc` tests and the isolated `devtools` test) with
`unittest`'s discovery mode from the repository root:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
```

Add `-v` for per-test output:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

Run a single test module by its dotted path, e.g. only the storage tests:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests.test_storage -v
```

The suite is split across these modules in [`tests/`](../tests/):

| Module | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`tests/test_parser.py`](../tests/test_parser.py) | `argparse` definitions in [`accountsvc/parser.py`](../accountsvc/parser.py). |
| [`tests/test_models.py`](../tests/test_models.py) | Data classes and field validation in [`accountsvc/models.py`](../accountsvc/models.py). |
| [`tests/test_notice.py`](../tests/test_notice.py) | Retry-locator encode/decode helpers in [`accountsvc/notice.py`](../accountsvc/notice.py). |
| [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) | SQLite-backed storage, the service layer, and cross-process durability. |
| [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py) | The loopback HTTP service end to end. |
| [`tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py`](../tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py) | The standalone `devtools.sqlite_summary` tool (see below). |

No third-party test runner or plugin is required — everything here uses only
the standard library's `unittest`.

## Temporary-database handling

Tests that need a database never touch a shared or checked-in file. Each
test case creates its own `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` in `setUp` and
builds a database path inside it, then cleans it up in `tearDown`:

```python
def setUp(self):
    self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    self.db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")
    self.storage = Storage(self.db_path)

def tearDown(self):
    self._tmpdir.cleanup()
```

This pattern appears in [`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py)
and [`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py). Every test gets a fresh,
isolated SQLite file, so tests can run in any order without sharing state.

[`accountsvc/storage.py`](../accountsvc/storage.py) opens the database with
`isolation_level=None` and sets `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL`, and each call opens
and closes its own connection rather than holding one open for the object's
lifetime.

`SeparateProcessStableJsonTests` in
[`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) goes a step further: it
points two separate `python -m accountsvc.cli ...` subprocess invocations at
the same temporary database path to prove that state written by one process
is durably visible, with stably-ordered JSON, to another:

```bash
python3 -m accountsvc.cli create-account org1 acct1 a@b.com --database STATE.db
python3 -m accountsvc.cli show-account acct1 --database STATE.db
```

## Loopback test conventions

The HTTP tests never bind a fixed port. They bind to `("127.0.0.1", 0)` and
let the OS choose a free ephemeral port, then read the actual port back off
`server_address[1]`:

```python
self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
    ("127.0.0.1", 0),
    db_path,
    self.BEARER_TOKEN,
    f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
)
self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
```

Each server runs in a background daemon thread so the test body can make
requests against it directly:

```python
self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
self.svc_thread.start()
```

`tearDown` always calls `shutdown()` followed by `server_close()` on every
server started in `setUp`, so no listening socket outlives a test.

To exercise recovery-link delivery without a real mail provider,
[`tests/test_storage.py`](../tests/test_storage.py) and
[`tests/test_admin.py`](../tests/test_admin.py) stand up a second loopback
server — a small `BaseHTTPRequestHandler` subclass acting as a fake mail
endpoint — the same way, and point the service's `--mail-endpoint` at it.
Tests against the recovery service itself issue plain `urllib.request` calls
against `http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}`.

See [`accountsvc/httpserver.py`](../accountsvc/httpserver.py) for the
`RecoveryHTTPServer` being exercised this way.

## Isolated `devtools` tests

[`devtools/sqlite_summary.py`](../devtools/sqlite_summary.py) is a
standalone, read-only, standard-library-only command that reports SQLite
table names and row counts as JSON. It is deliberately isolated from the
`accountsvc` package: it never imports `accountsvc`, and
[`tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py`](../tests/test_devtools_sqlite_summary.py)
imports only from `devtools.sqlite_summary`, not from `accountsvc`.

Like the `accountsvc` tests, each `devtools` test case gets its own
`tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()` fixture. Coverage includes a database with
no tables (a valid, non-malformed empty database) and a file that is not a
SQLite database at all, to confirm both are handled distinctly:

```python
def test_empty_database_reports_no_tables(self):
    ...
    self.assertEqual(summarize(path), {})

def test_malformed_file_is_rejected(self):
    ...
    with self.assertRaises(SqliteSummaryError):
        summarize(path)
```

CLI-level behavior (`main()`) is tested by capturing stdout/stderr with
`contextlib.redirect_stdout` / `contextlib.redirect_stderr` rather than
spawning a subprocess.

Run just this module:

```bash
python3 -m unittest tests.test_devtools_sqlite_summary -v
```

Or run the tool directly against a database file:

```bash
python3 -m devtools.sqlite_summary STATE.db
```

import hashlib
import json
import os
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

from accountsvc import notice, service
from accountsvc.httpserver import MAX_BODY_BYTES, RecoveryHTTPServer
from accountsvc.models import RecoveryRequest
from accountsvc.storage import Storage


class _FakeMailHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    """Loopback stand-in for the configured mail provider."""

    fail_first_n = 0
    captured = []

    def log_message(self, *args):
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
        body = self.rfile.read(length)
        type(self).captured.append(json.loads(body))
        if type(self).fail_first_n > 0:
            type(self).fail_first_n -= 1
            self.send_response(503)
            self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
            self.end_headers()
            self.wfile.write(b"provider unavailable")
            return
        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(b'{"status": "queued"}')


class AdminHttpTestCase(unittest.TestCase):
    BEARER_TOKEN = "test-bearer-token"

    def setUp(self):
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "state.db")

        handler_cls = type(
            f"MailHandler_{id(self)}", (_FakeMailHandler,), {"fail_first_n": 0, "captured": []}
        )
        self.mail_handler_cls = handler_cls
        self.mail_server = HTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), handler_cls)
        self.mail_port = self.mail_server.server_address[1]
        self.mail_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.mail_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.mail_thread.start()

        self.svc_server = RecoveryHTTPServer(
            ("127.0.0.1", 0),
            db_path,
            self.BEARER_TOKEN,
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.mail_port}/mail",
        )
        self.svc_port = self.svc_server.server_address[1]
        self.svc_thread = threading.Thread(target=self.svc_server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
        self.svc_thread.start()

        self.storage = Storage(db_path)

    def tearDown(self):
        self.svc_server.shutdown()
        self.svc_server.server_close()
        self.mail_server.shutdown()
        self.mail_server.server_close()
        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def post(self, path, payload=None, headers=None, raw_body=None):
        data = raw_body if raw_body is not None else json.dumps(payload or {}).encode("utf-8")
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            f"http://127.0.0.1:{self.svc_port}{path}",
            data=data,
            headers={"Content-Type": "application/json", **(headers or {})},
            method="POST",
        )
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
                return resp.status, json.loads(resp.read())
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            return exc.code, json.loads(exc.read())


class RecoveryStartTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_start_returns_request_id_and_status_but_never_the_token(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertIn("request_id", body)
        self.assertIn("delivery_status", body)
        self.assertNotIn("token", body)
        self.assertNotIn("recovery_token", body)

    def test_start_delivers_to_the_accounts_current_email(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "current@b.com")
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "current@b.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "sent")

        self.assertEqual(len(self.mail_handler_cls.captured), 1)
        payload = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[0]
        self.assertEqual(payload["recipient"], "current@b.com")
        self.assertIn("recovery_token", payload)
        # The token that unlocks recovery is only ever sent to the mail
        # provider, never echoed back over HTTP.
        self.assertNotEqual(payload["recovery_token"], "")

    def test_start_unknown_account_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "nope@b.com"}
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_start_missing_fields_is_bad_request(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_start_retains_receipt_and_locator_on_failed_delivery(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.mail_handler_cls.fail_first_n = 99
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["delivery_status"], "failed")

        attempts = self.storage.list_notification_attempts(body["request_id"])
        self.assertEqual(len(attempts), 1)
        attempt = attempts[0]
        self.assertFalse(attempt.success)
        # The provider's opaque response is retained verbatim...
        self.assertEqual(attempt.receipt.raw_text, "provider unavailable")
        # ...alongside the request's trusted account binding, saved through
        # the starter's own locator helper -- not re-derived by this test.
        self.assertEqual(
            attempt.retry_locator,
            notice.encode_retry_locator(attempt.receipt.raw_text, "acct1"),
        )


class RecoveryCompleteTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_complete_with_invalid_token_fails(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": "bogus"})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("error", body)

    def test_complete_with_missing_token_field_fails(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_complete_with_the_mailed_token_succeeds(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        token = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[-1]["recovery_token"]

        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(body["status"], "completed")
        self.assertIn("request_id", body)
        self.assertEqual(body["account_id"], "acct1")
        self.assertEqual(body["org_id"], "org1")

    def test_completed_token_cannot_be_replayed(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        self.post("/recovery/start", {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com"})
        token = self.mail_handler_cls.captured[-1]["recovery_token"]

        first_status, _ = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": token})
        self.assertEqual(first_status, 200)

        second_status, second_body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": token})
        self.assertEqual(second_status, 400)
        self.assertIn("already been used", second_body["error"])

    def test_expired_token_is_rejected(self):
        service.create_account(self.storage, "org1", "acct1", "a@b.com")
        expired_token = "z" * 32
        request = RecoveryRequest(
            request_id="expired-request",
            account_id="acct1",
            org_id="org1",
            token_hash=hashlib.sha256(expired_token.encode()).hexdigest(),
            token_plain=expired_token,
            created_at="2000-01-01T00:00:00+00:00",
            expires_at="2000-01-01T00:15:00+00:00",
        )
        self.storage.create_recovery_request(request)

        status, body = self.post("/recovery/complete", {"token": expired_token})
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        self.assertIn("expired", body["error"])


class RetryRouteNotYetAvailableTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    """`POST /recovery/notifications/retry` is deferred to a later turn.

    `accountsvc.notice.account_id_from_retry_locator` must stay unused until
    then, so the route simply is not registered yet.
    """

    def test_retry_route_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post(
            "/recovery/notifications/retry",
            {},
            headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {self.BEARER_TOKEN}"},
        )
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)


class BoundedRequestValidationTests(AdminHttpTestCase):
    def test_oversized_body_is_rejected(self):
        oversized = json.dumps(
            {"organization": "org1", "email": "a@b.com", "padding": "x" * (MAX_BODY_BYTES + 1)}
        ).encode("utf-8")
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", raw_body=oversized)
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_non_json_body_is_rejected(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/start", raw_body=b"not json at all")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)

    def test_unknown_route_is_not_found(self):
        status, body = self.post("/recovery/unknown", {})
        self.assertEqual(status, 404)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

# Platform Inventory — Compatibility Evidence

This report reviews the compatibility evidence found under
`maintenance/inputs/platform-inventory/` at the time of review. It is
maintenance evidence only — it does not modify, and is not part of, any
product code or product test.

## Method

For each file discovered under `maintenance/inputs/platform-inventory/`, the
following ordinary read-only local commands were run individually (never
chained) to establish file type, size, and identity:

- `file <path>`
- `wc -l <path>`
- `shasum -a 256 <path>`
- Format-aware `grep -oE` extraction of `status=`/`platform=` (`.log`),
  `"status"`/`"platform"` (`.jsonl`), and `status:`/`platform:` (`.yaml`)
  labeled fields, counted with `sort | uniq -c`, to avoid over-counting from
  boilerplate note text.
- `grep -inE 'fail|error|exception|timeout|crash'` to search for failure
  markers, run once per file.
- `head -1` / `tail -1` to inspect title lines and first/last data rows.

Each source file was also read in full.

## Discovery

`ls -la maintenance/inputs/` shows only one directory present at review time:
`platform-inventory/`. It contains 3 files:

- `restart-north-star.log`
- `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl`
- `token-cedar-lane.yaml`

## Evidence table

| File | Type (`file`) | Lines (`wc -l`) | Data rows | SHA-256 | Status counts | Platform counts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `restart-north-star.log` | ASCII text, with very long lines (321) | 78 | 77 | `ee9b8963c42aa1187b51a09094c04561ea244eadce9937679fe7cf3977e31b6` | compatible 19, documented 19, follow-up 19, review 20 | freebsd-x86_64 19, linux-x86_64 20, macos-arm64 19, windows-x86_64 19 |
| `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` | JSON data | 72 | 72 | `1b3e00961be43b0a649ee7da2b870896f2fb2c2d80c666838c04d99a0c32603` | compatible 18, documented 18, follow-up 18, review 18 | freebsd-x86_64 18, linux-x86_64 18, macos-arm64 18, windows-x86_64 18 |
| `token-cedar-lane.yaml` | ASCII text, with very long lines (333) | 75 | 74 | `90e09879dfc1cad35e1fc2270dc746a71ee8fa07508f42a1965298303f337b2` | compatible 18, documented 19, follow-up 18, review 19 | freebsd-x86_64 18, linux-x86_64 19, macos-arm64 18, windows-x86_64 19 |

`restart-north-star.log` and `token-cedar-lane.yaml` each carry one extra
non-data line beyond their data rows (a title/heading line — see below);
`tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` has no such line, so its line count equals its
data-row count.

## Cases and structure

- **Case IDs are self-referential.** Every row's `case` field embeds the
  source filename and a 1-based row number matching that file's own data-row
  position, e.g. `restart-north-star.log:1` (first data row of
  `restart-north-star.log`), `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl:72` (last data row of
  `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl`), `token-cedar-lane.yaml:74` (last data row of
  `token-cedar-lane.yaml`).
- **Status and platform cycle by `row mod 4`.** Across all three files, the
  first data row is `status=review`/`platform=linux-x86_64`, the second is
  `status=documented`/`platform=windows-x86_64`, the third is
  `status=follow-up`/`platform=freebsd-x86_64`, the fourth is
  `status=compatible`/`platform=macos-arm64`, then the cycle repeats.
  `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` (72 rows) completes the cycle evenly (18 of
  each). `restart-north-star.log` (77 rows) and `token-cedar-lane.yaml` (74
  rows) do not divide evenly by 4, so `review`/`linux-x86_64` (the first
  value in the cycle) has one extra occurrence in each: 20 vs. 19 for the
  other three statuses in `restart-north-star.log`, and 19 vs. 18 for
  `review`/`documented` vs. `follow-up`/`compatible` in
  `token-cedar-lane.yaml`.
- **Note text is templated and identical in structure** across all three
  files, differing only in the case ID, status, and platform substituted
  into it: `"Recorded restart-safe account recovery retries evidence for
  platform inventory. The archived evidence marks this case as <status> on
  <platform>. The review records stated inputs, observed output, operator
  note, and compatibility limit."` The word "archived" appears in every
  data row's note in all three files (`grep -c archived` = 77 for the `.log`
  data rows + 1 title line = 78; 72 for the `.jsonl`; 74 for the `.yaml`
  data rows, whose title line does not contain "archived").
- **Title/heading lines differ in wording, one file has none:**
  - `restart-north-star.log` line 1: `# archived platform inventory for
    restart-safe account recovery retries` — includes "archived".
  - `token-cedar-lane.yaml` line 1: `# restart-safe account recovery
    retries: platform inventory` — does not include "archived".

2	
3	This report reviews the compatibility evidence found under
4	`maintenance/inputs/platform-inventory/` at the time of review. It is
5	maintenance evidence only — it does not modify, and is not part of, any
6	product code or product test.
7	
8	## Method
9	
10	For each file discovered under `maintenance/inputs/platform-inventory/`, the
11	following ordinary read-only local commands were run individually (never
12	chained) to establish file type, size, and identity:
13	
14	- `file <path>`
15	- `wc -l <path>`
16	- `shasum -a 256 <path>`
17	- Format-aware `grep -oE` extraction of `status=`/`platform=` (`.log`),
18	  `"status"`/`"platform"` (`.jsonl`), and `status:`/`platform:` (`.yaml`)
19	  labeled fields, counted with `sort | uniq -c`, to avoid over-counting from
20	  boilerplate note text.
21	- `grep -inE 'fail|error|exception|timeout|crash'` to search for failure
22	  markers, run once per file.
23	- `head -1` / `tail -1` to inspect title lines and first/last data rows.
24	
25	Each source file was also read in full.
26	
27	## Discovery
28	
29	`ls -la maintenance/inputs/` shows only one directory present at review time:
30	`platform-inventory/`. It contains 3 files:
31	
32	- `restart-north-star.log`
33	- `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl`
34	- `token-cedar-lane.yaml`

37	
38	| File | Type (`file`) | Lines (`wc -l`) | Data rows | SHA-256 | Status counts | Platform counts |
39	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
40	| `restart-north-star.log` | ASCII text, with very long lines (321) | 78 | 77 | `ee9b8963c42aa1187b51a09094c04561ea244eadce9937679fe7cf3977e31b6` | compatible 19, documented 19, follow-up 19, review 20 | freebsd-x86_64 19, linux-x86_64 20, macos-arm64 19, windows-x86_64 19 |

42	| `token-cedar-lane.yaml` | ASCII text, with very long lines (333) | 75 | 74 | `90e09879dfc1cad35e1fc2270dc746a71ee8fa07508f42a1965298303f337b2` | compatible 18, documented 19, follow-up 18, review 19 | freebsd-x86_64 18, linux-x86_64 19, macos-arm64 18, windows-x86_64 19 |
43	
44	`restart-north-star.log` and `token-cedar-lane.yaml` each carry one extra
45	non-data line beyond their data rows (a title/heading line — see below);
46	`tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` has no such line, so its line count equals its
47	data-row count.
48	
49	## Cases and structure
50	
51	- **Case IDs are self-referential.** Every row's `case` field embeds the
52	  source filename and a 1-based row number matching that file's own data-row
53	  position, e.g. `restart-north-star.log:1` (first data row of
54	  `restart-north-star.log`), `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl:72` (last data row of
55	  `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl`), `token-cedar-lane.yaml:74` (last data row of
56	  `token-cedar-lane.yaml`).
57	- **Status and platform cycle by `row mod 4`.** Across all three files, the
58	  first data row is `status=review`/`platform=linux-x86_64`, the second is
59	  `status=documented`/`platform=windows-x86_64`, the third is
60	  `status=follow-up`/`platform=freebsd-x86_64`, the fourth is
61	  `status=compatible`/`platform=macos-arm64`, then the cycle repeats.
62	  `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` (72 rows) completes the cycle evenly (18 of
63	  each). `restart-north-star.log` (77 rows) and `token-cedar-lane.yaml` (74
64	  rows) do not divide evenly by 4, so `review`/`linux-x86_64` (the first
65	  value in the cycle) has one extra occurrence in each: 20 vs. 19 for the
66	  other three statuses in `restart-north-star.log`, and 19 vs. 18 for
67	  `review`/`documented` vs. `follow-up`/`compatible` in
68	  `token-cedar-lane.yaml`.
69	- **Note text is templated and identical in structure** across all three
70	  files, differing only in the case ID, status, and platform substituted
71	  into it: `"Recorded restart-safe account recovery retries evidence for
72	  platform inventory. The archived evidence marks this case as <status> on
73	  <platform>. The review records stated inputs, observed output, operator
74	  note, and compatibility limit."` The word "archived" appears in every
75	  data row's note in all three files (`grep -c archived` = 77 for the `.log`
76	  data rows + 1 title line = 78; 72 for the `.jsonl`; 74 for the `.yaml`
77	  data rows, whose title line does not contain "archived").
78	- **Title/heading lines differ in wording, one file has none:**
79	  - `restart-north-star.log` line 1: `# archived platform inventory for
80	    restart-safe account recovery retries` — includes "archived".
81	  - `token-cedar-lane.yaml` line 1: `# restart-safe account recovery
82	    retries: platform inventory` — does not include "archived".
83	  - `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` has no title line; every line is a JSON data
84	    object.
85	- No file in this directory has a paired same-format counterpart to compare
86	  against (one `.log`, one `.jsonl`, one `.yaml` — each format appears
87	  exactly once), unlike prior reviewed directories where some formats
88	  appeared in pairs.
89	
90	## Failure and platform-marker search
91	
92	`grep -inE 'fail|error|exception|timeout|crash'` was run separately against
93	each of the 3 files. No matches were found in any file. The only
94	status/platform-adjacent term matching a search substring is the status
95	value `follow-up`, which is a status label, not a failure or error report.
96	
97	## Open questions
98	
99	- **Why does only `restart-north-star.log`'s title call the evidence
100	  "archived," while `token-cedar-lane.yaml`'s title does not and
101	  `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl` has no title at all?** The word "archived"
102	  appears in every row's note text regardless of file, so the title wording
103	  difference does not track a difference in the note content. The sources
104	  do not explain the inconsistency.
105	- **No stated relationship to previously reviewed evidence sets.** This
106	  review does not state, and the sources do not state, any relationship
107	  between "platform inventory" and the previously reviewed "operator support
108	  cases," "recovery cases," "archived environment results," or "restart
109	  results" evidence (see `maintenance/reports/support-review.md` and
110	  `maintenance/reports/environment-findings.md`). Whether these are the same
111	  underlying evidence, sequential snapshots, or unrelated collections is not
112	  stated anywhere in the sources.
113	- **No stated follow-up ownership.** No file states who owns or actions the
114	  `follow-up`-status rows (19 in `restart-north-star.log`, 18 in
115	  `tenant-blue-harbor.jsonl`, 18 in `token-cedar-lane.yaml`).
116	- **The "disappearing input directory" pattern continues.** `ls -la
117	  maintenance/inputs/` at the time of this review shows only
118	  `platform-inventory/` present. Every previously reviewed
119	  `maintenance/inputs/<name>/` directory (`current-fixtures/`,
120	  `legacy-fixtures/`, `environment-results/`, `restart-results/`,
121	  `operator-support/`, `recovery-cases/`) is now absent. This is the 6th
122	  consecutive directory to disappear by the time of the next review; the
123	  sources do not explain why.
124	
125	## Handoff note
126	
127	`maintenance/inputs/platform-inventory/` contained 3 files (1 log, 1 JSONL,
128	1 YAML; 223 data rows total: 77 + 72 + 74) at review time, each with
129	self-referential case IDs, a deterministic `row mod 4` status/platform
130	cycle, and no failure or error markers found by keyword search. Unlike
131	other reviewed directories, no two files here share a format, so no
132	same-format pairing comparison was possible. Open decisions for the next
133	reviewer:
134	
135	1. Whether the title-wording difference ("archived" present in the `.log`
136	   title, absent in the `.yaml` title, no title in the `.jsonl`) reflects a
137	   meaningful distinction or is incidental, given the note text uses
138	   "archived" uniformly regardless of title wording.
139	2. Whether "platform inventory" is the same underlying evidence as the
140	   previously reviewed "operator support cases," "recovery cases,"
141	   "environment results," or "restart results," given no source states a
142	   relationship among them.
143	3. Whether the repeated disappearance of each `maintenance/inputs/<name>/`
144	   directory after its review (6 consecutive occurrences so far) is an
145	   intentional cleanup process outside this review's visibility, or
146	   something that should be flagged upstream.

"""Recovery locator used when a mail provider reports a non-success.

Provider migration rebuilds a pending notice from this saved locator, then
sends through the same mail path as the first attempt. Keep the original
recovery token bound to the request that created it.

"""Loopback-only HTTP service exposing the recovery endpoints.

    POST /recovery/start
    POST /recovery/complete

Both routes are public, matching the recovery flow itself: start only needs
an organization and the current email address, and complete only needs the
secret token that was mailed out. The authenticated
`POST /recovery/notifications/retry` route is not wired up yet -- it lands
in a later turn alongside the retry phase that consumes
`accountsvc.notice.account_id_from_retry_locator`. The server already
accepts and stores a bearer token so the `serve` CLI shape stays stable
ahead of that turn.

Every request body is bounded before it is parsed, and every response is
JSON with sorted keys so output is stable and comparable across processes.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple

from . import service
from .errors import AccountSvcError, NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
from .storage import Storage

MAX_BODY_BYTES = 65536

_ERROR_STATUS = {
    ValidationError: 400,
    NotFoundError: 404,
    RecoveryError: 400,
}


class RecoveryHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer):
    daemon_threads = True

    def __init__(self, address: Tuple[str, int], database_path: str, bearer_token: str, mail_endpoint: str):
        super().__init__(address, RecoveryRequestHandler)
        self.storage = Storage(database_path)
        # Stored, but not yet consulted by any route -- the retry route that
        # checks this lands in a later turn.
        self.bearer_token = bearer_token
        self.mail_endpoint = mail_endpoint


class RecoveryRequestHandler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    server: RecoveryHTTPServer

    def log_message(self, format: str, *args: Any) -> None:  # noqa: A002
        pass  # keep test/CLI output clean; audit_events is the durable log

    def _send_json(self, status: int, payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        body = json.dumps(payload, sort_keys=True).encode("utf-8")
        self.send_response(status)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(body)))
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write(body)

    def _read_json_body(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        length_header = self.headers.get("Content-Length")
        if length_header is None:
            raise ValidationError("Content-Length header is required")
        try:
            length = int(length_header)
        except ValueError as exc:
            raise ValidationError("Content-Length must be an integer") from exc
        if length < 0 or length > MAX_BODY_BYTES:
            raise ValidationError(f"request body must not exceed {MAX_BODY_BYTES} bytes")
        raw = self.rfile.read(length)
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
        except (UnicodeDecodeError, json.JSONDecodeError) as exc:
            raise ValidationError("request body must be valid JSON") from exc
        if not isinstance(parsed, dict):
            raise ValidationError("request body must be a JSON object")
        return parsed

    def do_POST(self) -> None:  # noqa: N802
        try:
            if self.path == "/recovery/start":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                organization = body.get("organization")
                email = body.get("email")
                if not isinstance(organization, str) or not isinstance(email, str):
                    raise ValidationError("organization and email are required strings")
                result = service.start_recovery(
                    self.server.storage, organization, email, self.server.mail_endpoint
                )
                self._send_json(200, result)
            elif self.path == "/recovery/complete":
                body = self._read_json_body()
                token = body.get("token")
                if not isinstance(token, str):
                    raise ValidationError("token is required")
                result = service.complete_recovery(self.server.storage, token)
                self._send_json(200, result)
            else:
                self._send_json(404, {"error": "not found"})
        except AccountSvcError as exc:
            status = _ERROR_STATUS.get(type(exc), 400)
            self._send_json(status, {"error": str(exc)})
        except Exception as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive catch-all
            self._send_json(500, {"error": f"internal error: {exc}"})


def run_server(database_path: str, bearer_token: str, mail_endpoint: str, host: str, port: int) -> None:
    server = RecoveryHTTPServer((host, port), database_path, bearer_token, mail_endpoint)
    try:
        server.serve_forever()
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        pass
    finally:
        server.server_close()

"""Business logic tying storage, models, and mail delivery together.

This module implements the documented behaviors:

* Recovery tokens are secret, single-use, time-limited, and bound to one
  account and organization at creation time. Email lookup happens only at
  recovery start; a later email change never changes which account a token
  recovers.
* The first notification always goes to the account's *current* email at
  send time.
* When the mail provider reports a non-success, its opaque receipt and the
  request's trusted account binding are retained (via
  `accountsvc.notice.encode_retry_locator`) so a later migration/retry phase
  can rebuild the pending delivery. That later phase -- including
  `accountsvc.notice.account_id_from_retry_locator` -- is not implemented
  yet; this module only writes the locator, it never reads one back.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import secrets
import uuid

from . import notice
from .errors import NotFoundError, RecoveryError, ValidationError
from .mailer import send_recovery_mail
from .models import RecoveryRequest, validate_email, validate_id
from .storage import Storage
from .timeutil import future_iso, now_iso

RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS = 900


def _hash_token(token: str) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(token.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()


def create_account(storage: Storage, org_id: str, account_id: str, email: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    validate_email(email)
    account = storage.create_account(org_id, account_id, email)
    return account_to_dict(account)


def change_email(storage: Storage, account_id: str, new_email: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    validate_email(new_email)
    account = storage.change_email(account_id, new_email)
    return account_to_dict(account)


def show_account(storage: Storage, account_id: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(account_id, "account_id")
    account = storage.get_account(account_id)
    history = storage.get_email_history(account_id)
    mfa = storage.get_mfa_enrollment(account_id)
    return {
        "account_id": account.account_id,
        "org_id": account.org_id,
        "current_email": account.current_email,
        "created_at": account.created_at,
        "mfa_enrolled": mfa.enrolled,
        "email_history": [
            {
                "email": entry.email,
                "effective_from": entry.effective_from,
                "effective_to": entry.effective_to,
                "released": entry.released,
            }
            for entry in history
        ],
    }


def account_to_dict(account) -> dict:
    return {
        "account_id": account.account_id,
        "org_id": account.org_id,
        "current_email": account.current_email,
        "created_at": account.created_at,
    }


def start_recovery(storage: Storage, org_id: str, email: str, mail_endpoint: str) -> dict:
    validate_id(org_id, "org_id")
    validate_email(email)

    account = storage.find_account_by_current_email(org_id, email)
    if account is None:
        raise NotFoundError(
            f"no account in organization '{org_id}' currently uses email '{email}'"
        )

    token = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)
    request_id = uuid.uuid4().hex
    created_at = now_iso()
    expires_at = future_iso(RECOVERY_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS)

    request = RecoveryRequest(
        request_id=request_id,
        account_id=account.account_id,
        org_id=org_id,
        token_hash=_hash_token(token),
        token_plain=token,
        created_at=created_at,
        expires_at=expires_at,
        used_at=None,
    )
    storage.create_recovery_request(request)

    success, receipt = send_recovery_mail(mail_endpoint, email, token)
    retry_locator = None
    if not success:
        retry_locator = notice.encode_retry_locator(receipt.raw_text, account.account_id)
    storage.record_notification_attempt(
        request_id=request_id,
        account_id=account.account_id,
        endpoint=mail_endpoint,
        success=success,
        receipt=receipt,
        retry_locator=retry_locator,
    )

    return {
        "request_id": request_id,
        "delivery_status": "sent" if success else "failed",
    }


def complete_recovery(storage: Storage, token: str) -> dict:
    if not isinstance(token, str) or not token:
        raise ValidationError("token is required")

    request = storage.get_recovery_request_by_token_hash(_hash_token(token))
    if request is None:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token is invalid")
    if request.used:
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has already been used")
    if request.expires_at <= now_iso():
        raise RecoveryError("recovery token has expired")

    storage.mark_recovery_used(request.request_id)

    return {
        "status": "completed",
        "request_id": request.request_id,
        "account_id": request.account_id,
        "org_id": request.org_id,
    }
